E01A.selected_capability: Load a snapshot once, record version(), and retain its Delta table provider for the report.
E01A.conditional_alternatives: Use load_version(v) for a repeatable later reconstruction; refresh/rebuild only when current results are required.
E01A.inputs: Table URL/storage context and a loaded snapshot at report start.
E01A.outputs: Arc<dyn TableProvider>; query execution yields Arrow batches at that snapshot.
E01A.effects: Log/file reads only; later writers do not refresh the retained provider.
E01A.errors: Log/protocol load errors; retained-file loss may surface during stream consumption.
E01A.unknowns: Repeatable logical snapshot does not reserve files against vacuum; historical retention is a separate requirement.

E01B.selected_capability: Refresh the table with update_incremental(None), rebuild table_provider(), and replace its registration in the reused context each polling cycle.
E01B.conditional_alternatives: Keep the old provider for repeatable reports; rebuild is required for current dashboard rows.
E01B.inputs: Existing SessionContext and a table handle sharing the correct log store.
E01B.outputs: Updated table snapshot and new registered provider, then current Arrow rows.
E01B.effects: Read latest log and replace caller session registration; no Delta write.
E01B.errors: Refresh/storage/protocol or scan failures; replacing a registration is not a concurrency synchronization protocol.
E01B.unknowns: Queries already planned against the old provider can retain old state; define polling boundaries. Test e01b proves old/new rows locally.

E02A.selected_capability: Use DataFusion's plain Parquet relation/provider with projection and filtering for immutable non-Delta files.
E02A.conditional_alternatives: Use a Delta provider if the directory is a Delta table whose log semantics must apply.
E02A.inputs: Plain Parquet directory, schema/discovery policy, SessionContext, requested columns and predicate.
E02A.outputs: DataFrame/logical query and resulting batches or stream.
E02A.effects: Read physical files; no transaction publication.
E02A.errors: Schema, file, planner and execution/stream errors.
E02A.unknowns: The Delta reference establishes the boundary; exact plain-Parquet options and performance are not qualified here.

E02B.selected_capability: Use DeltaTable::table_provider() or its Delta-aware scan rather than querying remaining Parquet files directly.
E02B.conditional_alternatives: Use raw Parquet only for deliberate physical-file inspection, accepting a different relation.
E02B.inputs: Loaded Delta snapshot and compatible session/store context.
E02B.outputs: Logical rows after log removes, deletion vectors and mapping; DataFusion query/stream.
E02B.effects: Read current active data according to Delta state.
E02B.errors: Protocol/mapping admission, missing-file and stream errors.
E02B.unknowns: Pin evidence shows raw Parquet can include logically deleted data; optimizer efficiency is not established.

E03A.selected_capability: At this pin use table_provider(), DataFrame::select_columns(&["id"]), then execute_stream(); consume batches incrementally.
E03A.conditional_alternatives: scan_table().with_columns(["id"]) is a returned-inferred public call path, but the partition-first fixture exposes a projection-order defect; use only with a matching regression check.
E03A.inputs: Loaded snapshot, compatible DataFusion context, requested logical field id.
E03A.outputs: SendableRecordBatchStream; inspect its schema and each batch before downcasting.
E03A.effects: Read-only; streaming consumption, without collecting the entire relation.
E03A.errors: Provider/planning errors and errors during try_next are separate.
E03A.unknowns: Incremental consumption is not a process-memory bound. Test e03a validates name/type/values on a partition-first layout.

E03B.selected_capability: Build/register a Delta table provider and compose the existing DataFusion join/filter query.
E03B.conditional_alternatives: Direct scan_table stream suits a consumer that does not need relational query composition.
E03B.inputs: Loaded table snapshot, existing SessionContext with the other source, logical join/filter expressions.
E03B.outputs: DataFrame/LogicalPlan, then Arrow stream or collected batches.
E03B.effects: Read snapshot files and the other source.
E03B.errors: Expression/type, planner, object-store and streaming errors.
E03B.unknowns: Provider freshness remains explicit and query performance needs representative measurements.

E04A.selected_capability: Supply the concrete SessionState through with_session_state(Arc::new(state)) after ensuring it has Delta's planner.
E04A.conditional_alternatives: Start with create_session()/a Delta-configured state and add the caller UDF/runtime policy if the original planner lacks Delta support.
E04A.inputs: Concrete state, required UDF registry and RuntimeEnv, Arrow batches or LogicalPlan.
E04A.effects: Executes with caller state, writes files and publishes a log version on success.
E04A.errors: A plain DataFusion planner may fail on MetricObserver; do not silently discard required caller capabilities.
E04A.unknowns: Concrete state preservation does not make an incompatible planner compatible; test distinguishing UDF and resource behavior.

E04B.selected_capability: Set SessionFallbackPolicy::DeriveFromTrait explicitly only if its derived runtime/config/function subset satisfies the caller contract.
E04B.conditional_alternatives: Use RequireSessionState to reject a wrapper when exact behavior is mandatory; require a concrete Delta-capable state. InternalDefaults can lose the required UDF.
E04B.inputs: Arc<dyn Session>, fallback policy, required runtime/functions and operation input.
E04B.outputs: Resolved operation session, then Result<DeltaTable, DeltaTableError>.
E04B.effects: Derives or rejects state before execution; successful write publishes.
E04B.errors: Wrapper rejection, lost function or missing planner are distinct failures.
E04B.unknowns: DeriveFromTrait is not a clone of arbitrary planner/catalog/custom Session semantics; UDF preservation alone does not prove complete policy equivalence.

E05A.conditional_alternatives: Use RecordBatchWriter for staged incremental ingestion with explicit publication; input-plan writing when DataFusion already owns the relation.
E05A.inputs: Owned table plus IntoIterator<Item=RecordBatch>; schema/protocol-compatible arrays.
E05A.outputs: Result<DeltaTable, DeltaTableError>, with the updated version.
E05A.effects: Write data files and publish a Delta log commit.
E05A.errors: Schema/value/constraint, planning/storage and transaction errors; later hook failures may follow publication.
E05A.unknowns: Append is the default, but specify intent. SaveMode::Ignore is not a tested dedup/skip mechanism.

E05B.conditional_alternatives: Materialize batches only when that resource tradeoff is deliberate; the deprecated with_input_execution_plan accepts Arc<LogicalPlan>, not a physical ExecutionPlan.
E05B.inputs: Existing table, existing optimized logical plan and Delta-capable state retaining source/UDF/runtime context.
E05B.effects: Execute the source plan, append files and publish a commit.
E05B.errors: Ordinary DataFusion planner can fail on Delta MetricObserver; missing UDF/source/runtime mappings can fail before publication.
E05B.unknowns: Test e05b appends UDF-produced row 104 while preserving row 1 and uses the caller's RuntimeEnv. No bounded-memory claim follows from plan input.

E06A.selected_capability: Write the replacement batch with SaveMode::Overwrite and no replace_where predicate.
E06A.conditional_alternatives: Use replace_where for a subset, or merge for key-dependent changes; SchemaMode::Overwrite only when schema replacement is intentional and supported.
E06A.outputs: Updated DeltaTable whose current relation is the new batch.
E06A.effects: Logically remove old data, write replacement files and publish; old bytes may remain.
E06A.unknowns: Overwrite does not reclaim disk; physical deletion belongs to retention/vacuum.

E06B.selected_capability: Use SaveMode::Overwrite plus with_replace_where("id >= 2"); reject replacement rows outside the predicate.
E06B.conditional_alternatives: Use full overwrite when every row is replaced; merge when source-target matching determines actions.
E06B.inputs: Existing table and replacement batches all satisfying id >= 2.
E06B.outputs: Updated DeltaTable; rows outside the predicate remain.
E06B.effects: Rewrite selected slice and publish one new version.
E06B.errors: Out-of-predicate input fails validation; inspect observed version to establish no publication for this failure.
E06B.unknowns: Test e06b rejects [0,20] without version advance and replaces [2,3] with [20] while preserving id 1. Other partition/schema combinations need their own evidence.

E07A.selected_capability: Keep schema evolution disabled and reject incompatible input; explicitly compare the required schema if exact field/type identity is the application contract.
E07A.conditional_alternatives: Use SchemaMode::Merge only when evolution is intended; use a deliberate cast policy when compatible conversions are acceptable.
E07A.inputs: Fixed table schema and incoming batches including actual nullability/nested value constraints.
E07A.outputs: Successful unchanged-schema table, or a rejected write.
E07A.effects: Successful append publishes; validation failure may leave unreferenced files but must not be assumed committed.
E07A.errors: Wider/incompatible schemas, invalid values and constraints fail at separate points. with_cast_safety(false) errors on invalid tested casts; true may substitute null.
E07A.unknowns: Default compatibility/casting is not identical to strict Arrow schema equality; test required invariants and nullability explicitly.

E07B.selected_capability: Append with SchemaMode::Merge to admit compatible additive columns.
E07B.conditional_alternatives: Use ordinary append to enforce the existing schema; SchemaMode::Overwrite belongs to full overwrite and does not express preservation of old rows.
E07B.inputs: Existing table plus wider batch; verify supported schema/protocol/mapping configuration.
E07B.outputs: Updated table/schema; existing rows preserved with null in compatible new nullable fields.
E07B.effects: Append data and update metadata/protocol as required, publishing a commit.
E07B.errors: Incompatible evolution or mapped-table restrictions can reject before publication.
E07B.unknowns: Retained evidence covers additive nullable fields; nested evolution, required non-null additions and all mapping combinations are not certified.

E08A.selected_capability: DeltaTable::merge(source_df, qualified_key_equality) with explicit aliases, matched-update and unmatched-insert clauses.
E08A.conditional_alternatives: Use append for pure additions or replace_where for a complete replacement slice.
E08A.inputs: DataFrame source with unique non-null keys, target snapshot, qualified join and ordered rules.
E08A.effects: Rewrite/add/remove logical rows and publish; metrics describe actions.
E08A.unknowns: Assert final rows and inserted/updated counts; successful merge does not establish a persistent unique-key constraint.

E08B.selected_capability: Normalize duplicate keys with an explicit deterministic application rule, or reject them, before merge; define null-key semantics separately.
E08B.conditional_alternatives: Ordinary equality leaves null keys unmatched; a deliberate null-safe predicate changes matching. Deduplication is only appropriate with a specified tie-break policy.
E08B.inputs: Source multiplicity/nulls, target keys and clause ordering.
E08B.outputs: Normalized DataFrame then merge table/metrics, or explicit validation error.
E08B.errors: The tested duplicate matched updates error without advancing version; do not generalize to all duplicate-delete/unmatched-insert combinations.
E08B.unknowns: Verify duplicates in both source and target, null behavior, first-applicable clause ordering and conflict handling.

E09A.conditional_alternatives: Plain append when no coordination marker is required; use explicit replay reconciliation for uncertain prior results.
E09A.inputs: Stable application ID/version, batch input and optional diagnostic commit metadata.
E09A.outputs: Updated DeltaTable plus persisted txn action observable through transaction_version.
E09A.effects: Publish rows and coordination metadata in the commit.
E09A.errors: Write/commit/post-commit failures must be classified before retry.
E09A.unknowns: A marker records coordination state; it is not an automatic once-only write guarantee at this pin.

E09B.selected_capability: After losing a result, refresh independently and inspect transaction_version, commit metadata/history and data outcome before deciding to retry.
E09B.conditional_alternatives: If the marker and batch identity prove publication, acknowledge/skip the replay; if absent under exclusive ownership and retained evidence, retry. Ambiguous/mismatched evidence requires reconciliation. Stronger concurrency needs explicit ownership/coordination or a carefully specified domain-key merge.
E09B.inputs: Stable app/batch identity, source offsets, retained log/txn state and an ownership protocol.
E09B.outputs: Replay/skip/reconcile decision; only a justified retry invokes write.
E09B.effects: Reads committed state; an unsafe retry can append duplicates even with the same marker.
E09B.errors: Storage/transaction/hook uncertainty differs from an already observed marker; retention can erase evidence.
E09B.unknowns: Pre-read then append is not atomic. Local stale-marker conflict evidence is not distributed exactly-once. Test e09b shows skip after reconciliation and duplicate rows from a naive sequential retry.

E10A.selected_capability: Correct the validation failure, verify the observed log version remains unchanged, and resubmit the corrected operation.
E10A.conditional_alternatives: Use reload/reconciliation when failure phase is not known to precede publication.
E10A.inputs: Original version, validation error, corrected rows/schema/predicate and an independent observer.
E10A.outputs: A corrected successful table or another explicit validation error.
E10A.effects: The rejected transaction is unpublished; staged orphan files may remain and require retention policy.
E10A.errors: Do not retry invalid input unchanged or treat every generic error as pre-publication.
E10A.unknowns: Version stability is observed evidence for the particular failure, not a universal property of all error returns.

E10B.selected_capability: Treat the hook error as an ambiguous commit: independently refresh and reconcile version, application marker, metadata and resulting rows before replay.
E10B.conditional_alternatives: Retry only when non-publication is established under the application's ownership policy; repair/retry post-commit work separately when the data commit is already visible.
E10B.inputs: Operation identity, previous version, hook phase and retained committed evidence.
E10B.effects: A before_post_commit_hook failure can follow visible log publication; duplicate replay is a material risk.
E10B.errors: Error return does not establish rollback; backend publication and post-commit failures have different meanings.
E10B.unknowns: Local visibility evidence does not prove power-loss durability or remote backend atomicity.

E11A.selected_capability: Load/refresh the current table and use a Delta provider or scan_table stream for its snapshot contents.
E11A.conditional_alternatives: Use CDF for incremental row changes with operation metadata, not for current-state reconstruction by default.
E11A.inputs: Loaded current snapshot and session/storage context.
E11A.unknowns: Current means the explicit load/refresh point; retained providers are not live subscriptions.

E11B.selected_capability: Use scan_cdf().with_starting_version(start).with_ending_version(end) and DeltaCdfTableProvider::try_new for a DataFusion relation.
E11B.conditional_alternatives: Use CdfLoadBuilder::build(session, filters) for a physical plan with explicit execution/residual handling; a snapshot scan does not return change history.
E11B.inputs: CDF-enabled retained interval; inclusive explicit versions and supported table features.
E11B.outputs: Change rows with _change_type, _commit_version and _commit_timestamp; preserve insert/delete/update_preimage/update_postimage. The executed consumer observed UInt64 commit versions and Timestamp(Millisecond, None) commit timestamps; inspect and decode actual array types.
E11B.effects: Read log and change/data files; checkpoint the processed interval only after downstream success.
E11B.errors: Unrecorded/disabled CDF, invalid bounds, column mapping, missing files and planning/stream errors are distinct.
E11B.unknowns: Test e11b covers insert, update images and delete across versions 1..=3. It does not qualify timestamp boundaries or downstream exactly-once processing.

E12A.selected_capability: Read the explicit inclusive CDF interval through DeltaCdfTableProvider or CdfLoadBuilder::build.
E12A.conditional_alternatives: Use snapshot comparison or a separate application log if required changes are unavailable, with a different recovery contract.
E12A.inputs: Starting/ending versions fully inside retained historically enabled CDF.
E12A.outputs: Changes with commit metadata and both update images as applicable.
E12A.effects: Read-only; downstream checkpoint follows successful processing.
E12A.errors: Retention races, missing files, mapping restrictions and planner failures remain possible.
E12A.unknowns: Current enablement alone is insufficient evidence; confirm enablement across the requested history.

E12B.selected_capability: Inspect current head and historical CDF enablement, then bound the processed interval to actually available commits.
E12B.conditional_alternatives: Wait/retry later for future commits; for pre-enablement history use an explicit bootstrap snapshot/application recovery contract rather than fabricate missing changes.
E12B.inputs: Requested interval, observed head, enablement history and retained files.
E12B.outputs: Available CDF rows or explicit unavailable/empty-range decision.
E12B.effects: Read-only; persist only the successfully processed observed end.
E12B.errors: At this pin beyond-head ending versions clamp even without opt-in; beyond-head start normally rejects unless allow_out_of_range permits empty. Crossing earlier disabled history fails.
E12B.unknowns: Do not checkpoint the requested future end. All timestamp/transition combinations are not exhaustively tested.

E13A.selected_capability: Use table.optimize().with_type(OptimizeType::Compact) for many small live files.
E13A.conditional_alternatives: Use ZOrder(columns) when measured filtering patterns justify clustering; leave layout unchanged when rewrite cost exceeds benefit.
E13A.effects: Rewrite files and publish layout changes, possibly no-op on repeated runs; preserve logical rows.
E13A.unknowns: Measure file counts and real scan metrics; local row-preservation evidence does not establish a speedup or exact target file sizes.

E13B.selected_capability: Preview table.vacuum().with_dry_run(true) with explicit mode and retention policy.
E13B.conditional_alternatives: Use Lite for tracked tombstones; Full to consider eligible untracked orphans; optimize changes live layout and is not disk reclamation.
E13B.inputs: Loaded table, safe retention interval and required historical/CDF readership.
E13B.outputs: Result<(DeltaTable, VacuumMetrics), DeltaTableError>; inspect candidate paths.
E13B.effects: Preview performs no deletion; actual vacuum physically removes eligible objects. Defaults are dry_run=false and Lite.
E13B.errors: Retention enforcement rejects unsafe short intervals; missing historical data may later fail scan consumption.
E13B.unknowns: Choose retention for active readers and recovery. Cloud listing/deletion behavior is unqualified.

E14A.selected_capability: Clone/build a separate table handle and load_version(0), then query that historical provider.
E14A.conditional_alternatives: Use restore only when a new current version must be published.
E14A.inputs: Table/log context and retained version-0 files.
E14A.outputs: Historical DeltaTable snapshot and its rows.
E14A.effects: Read-only version selection; no current-head commit.
E14A.errors: Metadata load can succeed while later data reads fail after vacuum.
E14A.unknowns: An already loaded provider builder's version option may lose to its existing snapshot; select version on the table before building the provider.

E14B.selected_capability: table.restore().with_version_to_restore(0).await to publish a new head with version-0 data state.
E14B.conditional_alternatives: Use load_version(0) for a read-only historical view; a checkpoint only accelerates reconstruction.
E14B.inputs: Current table plus retained version-0 data and compatible protocol.
E14B.outputs: Result<(DeltaTable, RestoreMetrics), DeltaTableError>; new monotonically later commit.
E14B.effects: Publish restore history while retaining prior versions subject to retention.
E14B.errors: Missing historical files and protocol constraints can prevent restore; restore cannot recreate deleted bytes.
E14B.unknowns: Test e14b verifies v0 -> v1 -> restored v2 and keeps v1's two-row state readable.

E15A.selected_capability: Check consumer Cargo features, table protocol and ordinary Delta provider preconditions; the pinned mapped-column fixture reads logical names successfully.
E15A.conditional_alternatives: Use the feature/operation matrix for discovery; use raw Parquet only for physical inspection, where physical mapped names differ.
E15A.inputs: Column-mapped table snapshot and exact pinned profile.
E15A.outputs: Normal logical Delta rows or operation-specific admission error.
E15A.errors: Unsupported protocol/Cargo profile, mapping configuration and data access errors remain separate.
E15A.unknowns: The successful scan fixture is evidence for that path, not every mapped-schema evolution or operation.

E15B.selected_capability: Treat CDF separately: this pin's CDF build rejects non-None column mapping, despite ordinary scan support.
E15B.conditional_alternatives: Use a supported change source or explicitly designed snapshot comparison/recovery approach; do not strip mapping metadata to force access.
E15B.inputs: Mapped table and requested historically enabled CDF interval.
E15B.outputs: Operation-specific rejection rather than a supported CDF relation.
E15B.effects: No successful CDF output; no table mutation is justified by feature recognition.
E15B.errors: Recognized feature names and checker acceptance are weaker than the CDF operation precondition.
E15B.unknowns: Future versions may change this cell; rerun exact-profile operation probes before claiming support.

E16A.selected_capability: Ensure the session has the table's correct root store mapping before execution; Delta registration helpers populate missing mappings.
E16A.conditional_alternatives: Register explicitly through RuntimeEnv::register_object_store(root_url, root_object_store) when the caller owns store setup.
E16A.inputs: Compatible Session runtime, table LogStore root URL and correctly scoped root object store.
E16A.outputs: Configured object-store registry, then executable provider/plan.
E16A.effects: Mutates caller runtime configuration; performs object I/O on execution.
E16A.errors: URL/prefix mismatch, credentials and absent backend features can still fail.
E16A.unknowns: Automatic check-and-register is not atomic concurrency coordination and will not repair an existing wrong mapping.

E16B.selected_capability: Explicitly replace the stale mapping with RuntimeEnv::register_object_store(table.log_store().root_url(), table.log_store().root_object_store(None)).
E16B.conditional_alternatives: Keep the existing mapping only after establishing it is the intended store; an absent mapping can use normal helper registration.
E16B.inputs: Caller runtime, target root URL, trusted table root store and coordination over shared registry changes.
E16B.outputs: Repaired mapping and successful reads through the provider.
E16B.effects: Replaces shared runtime routing; ordinary registration helpers preserve old mappings.
E16B.errors: Wrong mappings survive provider setup and fail execution; prefix and root scope must be correct.
E16B.unknowns: Test e16b proves failure through the bad store and success after explicit replacement; concurrent registry mutation is not qualified.

H01.selected_capability: Prefer DeltaCdfTableProvider with a DataFusion filter; its scan enforces a row-level residual.
H01.conditional_alternatives: With lower-level CdfLoadBuilder::build, wrap the resulting plan in an exact residual FilterExec as required; internal builder filter state is only a partition-pruning lead.
H01.inputs: CDF interval, non-partition predicate, compatible Session/TaskContext and PhysicalExpr when using low-level execution.
H01.outputs: Only predicate-matching change rows, preserving change metadata.
H01.effects: Read-only; file pruning reduces candidates but cannot establish row-level correctness.
H01.errors: Planning/type errors, disabled/missing CDF and mapping restrictions remain material.
H01.unknowns: Retained provider test filters id > 5 to the update postimage. Verify all predicate columns remain available and do not assume a pushed expression was fully applied.

H02.selected_capability: Treat Arrow/kernel conversion, value casting, Delta normalization and schema evolution as separate operations.
H02.conditional_alternatives: Use existing compatible schema for fixed writes; SchemaMode::Merge only for intentional supported evolution; reject lossy casts when null substitution is unacceptable.
H02.inputs: Nullable nested arrays/schema, timestamp units/timezone, exact Cargo feature profile and table protocol.
H02.outputs: Normalized Delta schema and persisted values; conversion errors remain explicit.
H02.effects: Normalization/casting can alter schema meaning; writes may update metadata/protocol and publish.
H02.errors: Test nested parent/child nulls, invalid non-null values, timestamp precision/ranges/timezones and protocol feature admission.
H02.unknowns: The reference proves nested decimal schema fidelity but nanosecond UTC normalizes to microseconds and UInt64 schema round-trips Int64 in its profile. It does not prove all actual value conversions are lossless.

H03.selected_capability: Choose Full vacuum to discover eligible untracked orphan files, with_dry_run(true), safe retention and with_keep_versions for required historical snapshots.
H03.conditional_alternatives: Lite derives candidates from tracked tombstones and will miss untracked orphans; leave files when necessary history/readers cannot be protected.
H03.inputs: Explicit mode, age/retention policy, required versions and retained log/data availability.
H03.outputs: Preview candidates/VacuumMetrics; after reviewed policy, actual removal results.
H03.effects: Full lists storage; actual vacuum removes bytes and can invalidate historical/CDF reads.
H03.errors: Retention guards, missing retained history, permissions/listing/deletion errors.
H03.unknowns: keep_versions is experimental and not indefinite retention; test the protected versions by consuming their data after cleanup. Remote backend behavior remains unqualified.

H04.selected_capability: Use built-in deltalake-catalog-glue or deltalake-catalog-unity for identity discovery; DataCatalog::get_table_storage_location returns the storage location.
H04.conditional_alternatives: Use UnityCatalogList/UnityCatalogProvider/UnitySchemaProvider for DataFusion catalog/schema/table integration; direct URLs suffice when already resolved.
H04.inputs: Catalog/database/table IDs plus exact adapter features and authentication options.
H04.outputs: Resolved storage URL, or DataFusion catalog/provider objects; then load using appropriate storage adapters.
H04.effects: Catalog service lookups followed by storage/log access; provider freshness requires a caller policy.
H04.errors: Not-found/auth/service errors differ from storage credentials, table protocol and query errors.
H04.unknowns: Live Glue/Unity, cloud auth and catalog caching/freshness are not runtime-qualified by these local tests. Catalog access does not prove table-read compatibility.

H05.selected_capability: RecordBatchWriter::for_table(&table), write batches, then explicitly publish through flush_and_commit(&mut table).
H05.conditional_alternatives: Use high-level DeltaTable::write for a complete write-and-commit operation; use flush actions with CommitBuilder only if you own correct transactional semantics.
H05.inputs: Loaded table/schema, incoming RecordBatches and mutable writer/table handle for publication.
H05.outputs: write buffers input; flush returns Add actions/staged files; flush_and_commit returns a committed Version.
H05.effects: File staging is not log visibility; only publication makes rows part of a Delta snapshot.
H05.errors: Write/flush failure may leave unreferenced files; publication or post-commit error needs reconciliation before replay.
H05.unknowns: The reader's visibility probe sees new rows only after commit. Do not flush and discard Add actions, then assume a later empty flush commits previously returned actions.

H06.selected_capability: Reopen the capability decision when the refreshed candidate surface adds a relevant built-in, even if the old selected signature is unchanged.
H06.conditional_alternatives: Retain the current recommendation only after comparing conditions, tradeoffs and evidence against the new built-in.
H06.inputs: New immutable capture/revision, lock/features, neighboring candidates and old decision/claims.
H06.outputs: Reviewed alternatives/recommendation plus refreshed evidence and invalidation record.
H06.effects: Regenerate from authoring/captures; rerun affected consumer/probe assertions and retain old identities.
H06.errors: Unlinked semantic changes can escape automatic invalidation; absent matches do not prove no impact.
H06.unknowns: scripts/invalidation.py supplies review hints across selected contracts, source, profiles and neighboring candidate surfaces; it is not a proof of semantic equivalence.
